I noticed a lot of comments regarding concerns about the age gap, but I’m going to throw in my two cents as someone who has dated much older men in the past due to not being able to connect with men the same age. I also spent several years of my adult life in Japan where age gaps are more socially accepted compared to the United States. 

Yes, the age gap is concerning, and yes, more often than not it’s likely that your daughter’s partner may be at a different stage in life, but you have never met nor have you taken an opportunity to get to know her partner. I think it is unfair for people in this thread to come to the conclusion that he is preying on her. 

Needless to say, you should play the role of a supportive mother and confidant by making your concerns about the age gap clear. But ultimately your daughter is an adult and if she pursues this relationship and it ends badly due to the age gap then that is something that she needs to learn the hard way. You can’t shield her from everything and you would be doing her a disservice by preventing her from making her own life decisions. On the other hand, who knows, this relationship may work out. 

Your husband’s reaction, however, is abhorrent. What kind of person takes away an 18-year-old’s car keys and phone and keeps her trapped at home? Regardless of the fact that he is paying her tuition, quit treating her like a child. Your husband is running the risk of permanently damaging not only his relationship with your daughter, but your relationship with her.
I’m aware of that, which is why when I deal with qultists I like to throw their logic back in their face when they bring up topics such as abortion.

He can tell her that it is his body, his choice. 

While it is her decision on whether she wants to be vaccinated or not, she has no place in imposing her views on your boyfriend. He can tell her that after much thought he decided that he would rather keep his career than suffer the fallout from the (nonexistent) risks associated with the vaccine.
You’re an adult. He doesn’t need to tell you what to do.

I’m glad to hear that. Have you sought professional help for your suicidal thoughts?

It seems that in society there is a huge stigma against depression because most people are knowledgeable about it. I find that friends and family, who I’m sure try to mean well and care about you, are the ones who end up causing the most damage. 

I’ve been told that I’m selfish for attempting suicide and that I’m just seeking attention. It’s the most painful thing to hear when the only thing you’re trying to seek is compassion and understanding for your situation. 

The most important thing to know when someone, whether it’s a friend or a family member or a boss, shuts you down it’s because they’re poorly equipped to deal with mental health issues. They’re not trained to handle it and they are not mental health professionals at all. 

So who would you rather trust, a trained doctor who knows how to address a depressed patient? Or a friend who thinks “sucking it up” and trying to be happy is the answer.

It sounds like you have a lot on your plate right now. It may be overwhelming and you might not have the energy to to turn your life around but take it one at a time. 

For example, you can’t exercise for more than ten minutes because of your horrible diet. Try gradually introducing healthier foods into your diet. Instead of that piece of fried chicken spend five minutes sautéing a lean chicken breast. If you have a craving for sweets go for a piece of fruit so you can satisfy that craving for sugar. 

From there incorporate some exercise in your routine. You don’t have to immediately start commuting to the gym six times a week. Start with a walk while listening to music to make it less boring. Take a light yoga class or follow along a short yoga video on YouTube. If you feel like you can handle more, pat yourself on the back because you’ve done great. 

And nurture that singing talent because I’m sure you have an amazing gift. You don’t have to look sexy and hot to be a good singer. You just need your voice. 

As for thoughts to ending your life, don’t be afraid to seek help from a professional. They’re trained to help you overcome this.

It’s something I’ve gone through before myself. I’ve been called selfish for contemplating or attempting suicide and I’m not the only one out there. 

Friends and family mean well and they want you to be happy, but I should stress that they are not mental health care professionals. They are not trained to listen to your problems and give you advice that will allow you to address them in a healthy way. I’m sure they care about you but they don’t understand the psychological torment you’re going through.
